sections.overview: The ruddy cuckoo-dove is a reddish-brown pigeon native to Brunei, Indonesia and Malaysia.
sections.identification: Its overall rufous-brown plumage and paler yellowish head help distinguish it from other cuckoo-doves.
sections.habitat: It inhabits forest, wooded country and tree-rich plantations in lowlands and foothills.
sections.diet: Species accounts describe quiet foraging in the middle and lower forest layers, but the sources consulted do not establish a detailed diet.
sections.behavior: It is shy and unobtrusive, usually feeding within forest cover and giving a repeated, low, cooing call.
sections.reproduction: The concise species accounts consulted provide no reliable detail on nesting or breeding timing.
sections.ecology: The Enggano Cuckoo-Dove (Macropygia cinnamomea), once grouped with it, is now treated as a separate species partly on the basis of plumage and voice.
sections.conservation: Oiseaux.net reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern; that category does not mean every local population is secure.
